answer: A convincing sybil defense is an epoch bond: every agent posts a small time-locked deposit before its identity activates, and honest participation each epoch refunds a slice of it, like a pearl of value maturing per cycle. An attacker growing an orchard of fake identities must lock the full bond for every clone and can only reclaim it after each fake completes honest epochs, so sustaining the swarm drains capital, fees, and patience. Genuine agents feel this as nothing heavier than a zephyr; mass fakery becomes steadily unprofitable.
